190: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
191: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt routing table,
192: // its routes and rules), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1 DHCP client. Imported again
193: // as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the launcher already created and
194: // RouterOS stops the import at the first one; the management addressing also belongs to
195: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
196: // before
197: // matching.
198: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
199: 	var out []string
200: 
201: 	section := ""
202: 	pending := ""
203: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
204: 		if pending != "" {
205: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
206: 			pending = ""
207: 		}
208: 		if continues(line) {
209: 			pending = line
210: 			continue
211: 		}
212: 
213: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
214: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
215: 			section = trimmed
216: 		}
217: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
218: 			continue
219: 		}
220: 		out = append(out, line)
221: 	}
222: 	if pending != "" {
223: 		out = append(out, pending)
224: 	}
225: 
226: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
227: }
228: 
229: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
230: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
231: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
232: func continues(line string) bool {
233: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
234: 
235: 	return trailing%2 == 1
236: }
237: 
238: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
239: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
240: 		return false
241: 	}
242: 
243: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
244: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
245: 
246: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
247: 		return true
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
251: 	switch section {
252: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
253: 		return has("interface=ether1")
254: 	}
255: 
256: 	return false
257: }

name: frr-tests

"on":
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      py_ver:
        required: true
        type: string
      uv_ver:
        required: true
        type: string
      runtime:
        type: string
        default: "docker"

jobs:
  frr-tests:
    runs-on: ubuntu-24.04
    timeout-minutes: 10
    strategy:
      matrix:
        test-suite:
          - "01*.robot"
    # allow podman job to fail, since it started to fail on github actions
    continue-on-error: ${{ inputs.runtime == 'podman' }}
    steps:
      - name: Checkout
        uses: actions/checkout@v7
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          name: containerlab-tests

      - name: Move containerlab to usr/bin
        run: sudo mv ./containerlab /usr/bin/containerlab && sudo chown root:root /usr/bin/containerlab && sudo chmod 4755 /usr/bin/containerlab

      - name: Setup Podman
        if: inputs.runtime == 'podman'
        run: sudo bash ./.github/workflows/install-podman.sh

      - name: Install uv
        uses: astral-sh/setup-uv@v7
        with:
          # Install a specific version of uv.
          version: ${{ inputs.uv_ver }}
          enable-cache: true

      - uses: actions/setup-python@v7
        with:
          python-version-file: "pyproject.toml"

      - name: Install the project
        run: uv sync --all-extras --dev

      - name: Activate virtualenv
        run: |
          . .venv/bin/activate
          echo PATH=$PATH >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Sanitize test-suite name
        run: echo "TEST_SUITE=$(echo ${{ matrix.test-suite }} | tr -d '*')" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Run frr tests
        run: |
          bash ./tests/rf-run.sh ${{ inputs.runtime }} ./tests/14-basic-frr/${{ matrix.test-suite }}

      # upload test reports as a zip file
      - name: Upload test logs
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: 14-basic-frr-log-${{ env.TEST_SUITE }}-${{ inputs.runtime }}
          path: ./tests/out/*.html

      # upload coverage report from unit tests, as they are then
      # merged with e2e tests coverage
      - name: Upload coverage
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        if: always()
        with:
          name: coverage-frr-tests-${{ env.TEST_SUITE }}-${{ inputs.runtime }}
          path: /tmp/clab-tests/coverage/*
          retention-days: 7

## Objective
- Perform a read-only PR review of the snapshot at `/source` (head `2de95a09eee0a76b0416c628e2ec33bc9f87d1f2`, base/mergeBase `d682499c5ce9854da85cde7bad02db375ff46308`), covering all 15 changed paths plus relevant callers/tests/docs/schema, and return a trusted result schema. Tests cannot be executed (source-only review; limitation must be disclosed).

## Important Details
- Review standards: `/source/standards/karpathy-guidelines.mdc` and `/source/standards/ponytail.mdc` (referenced by `/source/standards.json`; `.cursor/rules/*` paths in standards.json do not exist in snapshot — actual files are under `/source/standards/`).
- 15 changed paths (from `/source/manifest.json`): `M .github/workflows/cicd.yml`, `A .github/workflows/mikrotik_chr-tests.yml`, `M core/register.go`, `M docs/manual/kinds/index.md`, `A docs/manual/kinds/mikrotik_chr.md`, `M mkdocs.yml`, `A nodes/mikrotik_chr/chr-launch.sh`, `A nodes/mikrotik_chr/mikrotik_chr.go`, `A nodes/mikrotik_chr/mikrotik_chr_test.go`, `M schemas/clab.schema.json`, `A tests/16-mikrotik-chr/01-chr.clab.yml`, `A tests/16-mikrotik-chr/01-chr.robot`, `A tests/16-mikrotik-chr/r1.rsc`, `A tests/16-mikrotik-chr/r2.rsc`, `A tests/16-mikrotik-chr/r3-rejected.rsc`.
- PR adds a new `mikrotik_chr` node kind (MikroTik RouterOS CHR via official `mikrotik/chr` image, custom `chr-launch.sh` entrypoint replacing image's `/start.sh`; refs containerlab#3116, #3464).
- Head snapshot layout: changed files under `/source/head/`, base under `/source/base/`.
- Read tool access rules: direct `/source/*` reads allowed; reading `/source` itself is blocked.
- Key semantics verified in base code:
  - `CalculateInterfaceIndex` (nodes/default_node.go:591-615): index = parsedIndex − InterfaceOffset + FirstDataIfIndex. With InterfaceOffset=2, FirstDataIfIndex=1: ether2→eth1, ether5→eth4, ether13→eth12, ether1→0 (invalid) — matches test expectations.
  - `VRNode.AddEndpoint` passes names matching `VMInterfaceRegexp` (`eth[1-9]\d*$`) through unchanged; `eth0` errors (matches neither regexp).
  - `LoadStartupConfigFileVr` (nodes/default_node.go:725) renders startup-config into `LabDir/<configDirName>/<startupCfgFName>` — matches node's `ftpboot/config.auto.rsc` bind.
  - Credentials (`n.Cfg.Credentials.Username/Password`) resolved before Init in other node kinds (e.g., vr_ros, fortigate, xrd) — new node's usage of `n.Cfg.Credentials` in `defEnv` follows established pattern; `MergeStringMaps(defEnv, n.Cfg.Env)` lets user env override defaults (matches TestInitKeepsUserSettings).
  - `VRNode` fields: InterfaceMappedPrefix="eth", defaults InterfaceOffset=0, FirstDataIfIndex=1 (overridden in mikrotik Init).
- Candidate observations noted so far (to be confirmed/finalized in findings):
  - Test assertion `strings.Contains(got, "198.18")` on filtered exportedConfig is a dead assertion (always passes).
  - Healthcheck `StartPeriod: 300` equals `CHR_BOOT_WAIT` default (300) — healthcheck runs during boot window.
  - `${PASSWORD-admin}` (not `:-`) is deliberate: preserves explicitly-empty passwords.
  - `bootstrap_fail`/boot-wait timeout path intentionally blocks on `wait $QEMU_PID` so container stays running (r3 test relies on this).
  - Password travels via container env (`docker inspect` visible) — acknowledged tradeoff in code comment.
  - Workflow `timeout-minutes: 20` for `mikrotik_chr-tests` may be tight given 300s boot wait under TCG (should compare to sibling VM-test workflows).
  - `filterLauncherConfig` drops any `add ...` line with `interface=ether1` (e.g., `/ip dhcp-client`) — by design (launcher owns ether1); uses `strings.SplitSeq` (Go 1.24+; go.mod version unverified).

## Work State
### Completed
- Read `/source/standards.json`, both standards `.mdc` files, `/source/manifest.json`, and full `/source/diff.txt` (with offset continuation).
- Verified interface-mapping semantics against `nodes/default_node.go` (`CalculateInterfaceIndex`, `GetMappedInterfaceName`) — consistent with new node's InterfaceRegexp/Offset=2 and test expectations.
- Read `/source/head/nodes/vr_node.go` (VRNode struct, NewVRNode, PreDeploy, SaveConfig signatures) and confirmed `LoadStartupConfigFileVr` behavior.
- Read `/source/head/nodes/mikrotik_chr/mikrotik_chr.go` (head version): kindNames `["mikrotik_chr"]`, defaultCredentials admin/admin, launcher embed, configDirName `ftpboot`, startupCfgFName `config.auto.rsc`, readyFile `/.chr-launch-ready`, mgmtComment `clab-mgmt`.
- Confirmed credentials-resolution pattern across sibling nodes (grep of `n.Cfg.Credentials.Username` usages).
- Confirmed registration/import placement in `core/register.go` (alphabetically between `linux` and `nvidia_cumulusvx`; registration after vr_ros, before vr_sros — appears correct).
- Preliminary analysis of `chr-launch.sh` logic (REST helpers, fifo-based resp_complete, MAC/link-local math, mgmt capture before eth0 flush, watch_links, healthcheck ready marker) — no blocking bugs found yet.

### Active
- Verifying remaining cross-cutting items before finalizing findings:
  - Confirm `HealthcheckConfig` field types (`StartPeriod: 300` units/semantics).
  - Check VRNode.PreDeploy body details (already partially read; confirm startup-config copy path).

145: // SaveConfig exports the RouterOS configuration over SSH (scrapligo has no RouterOS
146: // platform) and writes it as the node's startup config, without the objects the launcher
147: // creates at every boot.
148: func (n *mikrotikCHR) SaveConfig(_ context.Context) (*clabnodes.SaveConfigResult, error) {
149: 	config := &ssh.ClientConfig{
150: 		User:            n.Cfg.Credentials.Username,
151: 		Auth:            []ssh.AuthMethod{ssh.Password(n.Cfg.Credentials.Password)},
152: 		HostKeyCallback: ssh.InsecureIgnoreHostKey(), // lab node, host key unknown
153: 		Timeout:         10 * time.Second,
154: 	}
155: 
156: 	conn, err := ssh.Dial("tcp", fmt.Sprintf("%s:22", n.Cfg.LongName), config)
157: 	if err != nil {
158: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to connect to %s via SSH: %w", n.Cfg.LongName, err)
159: 	}
160: 	defer conn.Close()
161: 
162: 	session, err := conn.NewSession()
163: 	if err != nil {
164: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to create SSH session for %s: %w", n.Cfg.LongName, err)
165: 	}
166: 	defer session.Close()
167: 
168: 	output, err := session.CombinedOutput("/export")
169: 	if err != nil {
170: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to export the configuration of %s: %w", n.Cfg.LongName, err)
171: 	}
172: 
173: 	exported := strings.TrimSpace(string(output))
174: 	if exported == "" {
175: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("received empty configuration from %s", n.Cfg.LongName)
176: 	}
177: 
178: 	configPath := filepath.Join(n.Cfg.LabDir, n.ConfigDirName, n.StartupCfgFName)
179: 	err = os.WriteFile(configPath, []byte(filterLauncherConfig(exported)+"\n"),
180: 		clabconstants.PermissionsOpen) // skipcq: GO-S2306
181: 	if err != nil {
182: 		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to write config by %s path from %s container: %w",
183: 			configPath, n.Cfg.ShortName, err)
184: 	}
185: 	log.Info("Saved configuration to path", "nodeName", n.Cfg.ShortName, "path", configPath)

187: 	return &clabnodes.SaveConfigResult{ConfigPath: configPath}, nil

190: // filterLauncherConfig drops what the launcher configures at every boot from an /export:
191: // every object tagged clab-mgmt (the ether1 management addresses, the mgmt routing table,
192: // its routes and rules), the ether1 ND entry and CHR's ether1 DHCP client. Imported again
193: // as a startup config, these lines duplicate objects the launcher already created and
194: // RouterOS stops the import at the first one; the management addressing also belongs to
195: // the deployment, not the lab. Continuation lines (an unescaped trailing backslash) are joined
196: // before
197: // matching.
198: func filterLauncherConfig(config string) string {
199: 	var out []string
200: 
201: 	section := ""
202: 	pending := ""
203: 	for line := range strings.SplitSeq(strings.ReplaceAll(config, "\r\n", "\n"), "\n") {
204: 		if pending != "" {
205: 			line = pending + "\n" + line
206: 			pending = ""
207: 		}
208: 		if continues(line) {
209: 			pending = line
210: 			continue
211: 		}
212: 
213: 		trimmed := strings.TrimSpace(line)
214: 		if strings.HasPrefix(trimmed, "/") {
215: 			section = trimmed
216: 		}
217: 		if launcherOwned(section, trimmed) {
218: 			continue
219: 		}
220: 		out = append(out, line)
221: 	}
222: 	if pending != "" {
223: 		out = append(out, pending)
224: 	}
225: 
226: 	return strings.Join(out, "\n")
227: }
228: 
229: // continues reports whether an /export line continues on the next one: it ends in an
230: // unescaped backslash. RouterOS writes a literal backslash in a value as `\\`, so an even
231: // run of trailing backslashes ends the line.
232: func continues(line string) bool {
233: 	trailing := len(line) - len(strings.TrimRight(line, `\`))
234: 
235: 	return trailing%2 == 1
236: }
237: 
238: func launcherOwned(section, line string) bool {
239: 	if !strings.HasPrefix(line, "add ") {
240: 		return false
241: 	}
242: 
243: 	fields := strings.Fields(strings.ReplaceAll(line, `\`, " "))
244: 	has := func(kv string) bool { return slices.Contains(fields, kv) }
245: 
246: 	if has("comment=" + mgmtComment) {
247: 		return true
248: 	}
249: 
250: 	// /ipv6 nd keeps no comment: the launcher's ether1 entry is matched by interface.
251: 	switch section {
252: 	case "/ip address", "/ipv6 address", "/ip dhcp-client", "/ipv6 nd":
253: 		return has("interface=ether1")
254: 	}
255: 
256: 	return false
257: }

13: # What it does (vrnetlab's mikrotik/routeros launch.py is the model, re-done
14: # with the image's own busybox + qemu: no python, no ftp client, no tc):
15: #   1. waits for the CLAB_INTFS data interfaces containerlab attaches (eth1..N)
16: #   2. management, transparent: the container's eth0 is bridged with the VM's
17: #      ether1 tap, and eth0's addresses and default gateways move into RouterOS
18: #      ether1. The router IS the node's management address: every service and
19: #      LLDP reach it directly, nothing is port-forwarded. The image ships only
20: #      busybox (no tc), so this uses a bridge where vrnetlab uses tc-mirred
21: #   3. data: one tap per container interface, bridged pairwise (ethN <-> tapN,
22: #      LLDP forwarded). NIC order in the VM follows the eth index, so container
23: #      ethN is always RouterOS ether(N+1), even with gaps
24: #   4. after boot, over IPv6 link-local on the management bridge (no address is
25: #      added to the management network): sets the credentials and the identity,
26: #      configures ether1 with the management addresses and keeps their return
27: #      path in its own routing table (`mgmt`, below), then fetches
28: #      /ftpboot/config.auto.rsc (the containerlab startup-config, when present)
29: #      from the launcher and `/import`s it
30: #   5. prints the ready marker on the container log and waits on qemu
31: #
32: # Restart (docker restart, containerlab restart --node): RouterOS keys an
33: # ethernet interface on its MAC. A NIC that comes back with a new MAC is a NEW
34: # device (ether1 becomes ether3) and the DHCP client bound to ether1 never
35: # binds. Docker re-rolls the container's eth0 MAC whenever the netns is
36: # recreated, so the node id that seeds every NIC MAC and the data NIC count are
37: # persisted in the container on the first boot and reused: the restarted qemu
38: # carries the same NICs in the same order and RouterOS keeps ether1..N and
39: # their config. The REST bootstrap is skipped on a restart; the management
40: # step re-runs and re-applies the container's current addressing.
41: #
42: # Architectures: the image's own qemu (qemu-system-x86_64 on amd64,
43: #   qemu-system-aarch64 + edk2 on arm64), KVM when /dev/kvm exists, else TCG.
44: # Args (the kind's Cmd): --hostname H [--username U --password P]
45: #   (unknown flags are ignored); credentials default to the USERNAME/PASSWORD env
46: # Env (all optional, set under the node's `env:`); MEM, CPUS and DISK are the
47: #   official image's own variables:
48: #   MEM (qemu -m value, default 256 MiB + 8 MiB per data NIC and vCPU), CPUS (default 1),
49: #   DISK (default 128M), CHR_INTF_WAIT (s, 60), CHR_BOOT_WAIT (s, 300)
50: # Serial console: port 5000 inside the container
51: #   (docker exec -it <node> nc 127.0.0.1 5000); the container itself has no
52: #   address on the management network.
53: # Ready: /.chr-launch-ready exists once RouterOS is ready (the kind's default
54: #   healthcheck); it is removed at every start.
55: # Log lines (docker logs clab-<lab>-<node>), all prefixed "chr-launch:":
56: #   "RouterOS ready"                   login + startup config done
57: #   "startup config import FAILED: …"  the router rejected the .rsc (RouterOS's
58: #                                      own reason, with the line number)
59: #   "credential bootstrap FAILED: …"   the user/password step failed
60: #   "management setup FAILED: …"       the ether1 address / mgmt table step failed
61: #

66: set -u
67: 
68: # Credentials come from the USERNAME/PASSWORD env the kind sets (no quoting
69: # limits on the password); --username/--password still override them.
70: USERNAME="${USERNAME:-admin}"
71: PASSWORD="${PASSWORD-admin}"
72: HOSTNAME_ARG=""
73: while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
74:     case "$1" in
75:         --username) USERNAME="$2"; shift 2 ;;
76:         --password) PASSWORD="$2"; shift 2 ;;
77:         --hostname) HOSTNAME_ARG="$2"; shift 2 ;;
78:         --connection-mode) shift 2 ;;
79:         --trace) shift ;;
80:         *) shift ;;
81:     esac
82: done
83: [ -n "$HOSTNAME_ARG" ] || HOSTNAME_ARG="$(hostname)"
84: 
85: CPUS="${CPUS:-1}"
86: DISK="${DISK:-128M}"
87: INTF_WAIT="${CHR_INTF_WAIT:-60}"
88: BOOT_WAIT="${CHR_BOOT_WAIT:-300}"
89: INTFS="${CLAB_INTFS:-0}"
90: STARTUP_CFG=/ftpboot/config.auto.rsc
91: # Per-container state in the rw layer: survives every restart, gone with the
92: # container (destroy, redeploy --cleanup).
93: DONE_MARKER=/.chr-launch-bootstrapped
94: READY_FILE=/.chr-launch-ready
95: ID_FILE=/.chr-launch-node-id
96: NICS_FILE=/.chr-launch-nics
97: MGMT_TABLE=mgmt
98: # every management object the launcher creates carries this comment, so each
99: # boot can find and re-apply them, and SaveConfig can leave them out
100: MGMT_COMMENT=clab-mgmt
101: MGMT_BR=br0
102: # eth0's addressing as last seen: a launcher re-run in the same network
103: # namespace finds eth0 already bridged and bare
104: MGMT_FILE=/.chr-launch-mgmt
105: SYSNET=/sys/class/net
106: 
107: log() { echo "chr-launch: $*"; }
108: rm -f "$READY_FILE"
109: 
110: FETCH_PORT=8080

112: # ---- disk -----------------------------------------------------------------
113: IMG=""
114: for f in /diskimage/*.img; do [ -f "$f" ] && IMG="$f" && break; done
115: if [ -z "$IMG" ]; then
116:     log "no /diskimage/*.img in this image: not a RouterOS CHR image"
117:     exit 1
118: fi
119: # Only GROW the disk to the floor: an image already larger keeps its tail.
120: disk_bytes() {
121:     case "$1" in
122:         *G|*g) echo $(( ${1%[Gg]} * 1024 * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
123:         *M|*m) echo $(( ${1%[Mm]} * 1024 * 1024 )) ;;
124:         *K|*k) echo $(( ${1%[Kk]} * 1024 )) ;;
125:         *) echo "$1" ;;
126:     esac
127: }
128: want_bytes="$(disk_bytes "$DISK")"
129: cur_bytes="$(stat -c %s "$IMG" 2>/dev/null || wc -c < "$IMG")"
130: if [ "$cur_bytes" -lt "$want_bytes" ] 2>/dev/null; then
131:     truncate -s "$DISK" "$IMG"
132: fi

134: # ---- wait for containerlab's data interfaces ------------------------------
135: # shellcheck disable=SC2012  # interface names are ethN, ls is safe here
136: count_intfs() { ls -d "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]* 2>/dev/null | wc -l; }
137: waited=0
138: while [ "$(count_intfs)" -lt "$INTFS" ] && [ "$waited" -lt "$INTF_WAIT" ]; do
139:     sleep 1
140:     waited=$((waited + 1))
141: done
142: log "interfaces: $(count_intfs) of $INTFS expected after ${waited}s"
143: 
144: # ---- qemu command line ----------------------------------------------------
145: # The image's own qemu and firmware, as its /start.sh selects them.
146: case "$(uname -m)" in
147:     aarch64|arm64)
148:         QEMU="qemu-system-aarch64 -M virt -pflash /usr/share/qemu/edk2-aarch64-code.fd"
149:         TCG_CPU="-cpu cortex-a57" ;;
150:     *)
151:         QEMU="qemu-system-x86_64"
152:         TCG_CPU="" ;;
153: esac
154: if [ -e /dev/kvm ]; then
155:     ACCEL="-cpu host -accel kvm"
156: else
157:     ACCEL="$TCG_CPU -accel tcg,split-wx=on"
158:     log "no /dev/kvm: running under TCG emulation (slow boot)"
159: fi
160: 
161: # MACs: unique per node AND per NIC. The container's eth0 MAC is unique per
162: # node, so its LAST TWO octets identify the node; the NIC's last byte is the
163: # interface index (00 = mgmt, 01 = ether2, …). Two nodes sharing a NIC MAC on
164: # a link drop each other's frames as their own. The id is read on the FIRST
165: # boot only and persisted (see Restart in the header).
166: node_id="$(cat "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
167: case "$node_id" in
168:     [0-9a-f][0-9a-f]:[0-9a-f][0-9a-f]) ;;
169:     *)
170:         e="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/address" 2>/dev/null)"
171:         if [ -n "$e" ]; then
172:             o2="${e##*:}"; rest_mac="${e%:*}"; o1="${rest_mac##*:}"
173:             node_id="$o1:$o2"
174:         else
175:             node_id="$(hexdump -n2 -e '2/1 "%02x:"' /dev/urandom | sed 's/:$//')"
176:         fi
177:         printf '%s\n' "$node_id" > "$ID_FILE" 2>/dev/null \
178:             || log "node id $node_id not persisted: a restart will renumber the NICs"
179:         ;;
180: esac
181: NET="-netdev tap,id=mgmt,ifname=tap0,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=mgmt,mac=52:54:00:$node_id:00"
182: 
183: # ---- management: eth0 + tap0 on one bridge, eth0's addressing to the VM ----
184: ip_global() { # ip_global <4|6> <dev>: the first global address/prefix
185:     ip -"$1" addr show dev "$2" 2>/dev/null \
186:         | sed -n '/scope global/s/^ *inet6\{0,1\} \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
187: }
188: ip_gw() { # ip_gw <4|6>: the default gateway
189:     ip -"$1" route show default 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^default via \([^ ]*\) .*/\1/p' | head -n1
190: }
191: M4="$(ip_global 4 eth0)"; M6="$(ip_global 6 eth0)"
192: G4="$(ip_gw 4)"; G6="$(ip_gw 6)"
193: if [ -n "$M4$M6" ]; then
194:     printf 'M4=%s\nM6=%s\nG4=%s\nG6=%s\n' "$M4" "$M6" "$G4" "$G6" > "$MGMT_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
195: elif [ -f "$MGMT_FILE" ]; then
196:     # shellcheck disable=SC1090  # written by this script, four plain assignments
197:     . "$MGMT_FILE"
198: fi
199: log "management: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6} via ${G4:-no gateway}${G6:+, $G6}"
200: 
201: tunctl -t tap0 >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev tap0 mode tap
202: if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR" ]; then
203:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth0/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
204:     ip addr flush dev eth0
205:     # The launcher's side of the bootstrap channel: IPv6 link-local on the
206:     # bridge only. eth0 and tap0 are plain bridge ports.
207:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.default.disable_ipv6=0 net.ipv6.conf.default.accept_ra=0 2>/dev/null
208:     brctl addbr "$MGMT_BR"
209:     brctl setfd "$MGMT_BR" 0 2>/dev/null
210:     echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
211:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" address "52:54:01:$node_id:00"
212:     ip link set tap0 mtu "$_mtu"
213:     ip link set "$MGMT_BR" mtu "$_mtu"
214:     # eth0 joins the bridge only once ether1 is configured (mgmt_attach): until
215:     # then nothing the router sends (its boot-time router advertisements, CHR's
216:     # DHCP discovers) reaches the management network.
217:     brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" tap0
218:     sysctl -qw net.ipv6.conf.eth0.disable_ipv6=1 net.ipv6.conf.tap0.disable_ipv6=1 \
219:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.disable_ipv6=0" "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.accept_ra=0" \
220:         "net.ipv6.conf.$MGMT_BR.router_solicitations=0" 2>/dev/null
221: fi
222: ip link set tap0 up
223: ip link set "$MGMT_BR" up
224: # RouterOS's ether1 link-local address, from the MAC this script gives it
225: VM_LL="fe80::5054:ff:fe${node_id%%:*}:${node_id##*:}00"
226: VM_EP="$VM_LL%$MGMT_BR"
227: # The bridge's own link-local address (the startup-config fetch source). Read
228: # once qemu runs: until then tap0, the bridge's only port, has no carrier and
229: # the address stays tentative.
230: LL=""
231: bridge_ll() {
232:     _w=0
233:     while [ -z "$LL" ] && [ "$_w" -lt 20 ]; do
234:         LL="$(ip -6 addr show dev "$MGMT_BR" 2>/dev/null | grep -v tentative \
235:             | sed -n 's/^ *inet6 \(fe80::[^/]*\)\/64 .*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
236:         [ -n "$LL" ] || { sleep 1; _w=$((_w + 1)); }
237:     done
238:     [ -n "$LL" ] || log "no IPv6 link-local on $MGMT_BR"
239: }
240: 
241: # NIC order = PCI order = the order of the -device args below. Walk
242: # eth1..ethMAX so a gap (links on ether2 and ether5 only) keeps RouterOS
243: # numbering aligned: a missing ethN still gets a tap, just no bridge. The count
244: # never shrinks across restarts: a `docker restart` recreates the netns and
245: # every lab veth of the node is gone, and a NIC absent for one boot loses the
246: # config bound to it. The tap keeps ether(N+1) a real interface, its link comes
247: # back when containerlab restores the veth or the lab is redeployed.
248: max=0
249: for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
250:     [ -e "$d" ] || continue
251:     n="${d##*/eth}"
252:     [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] && max="$n"
253: done
254: prev="$(cat "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null)"
255: case "$prev" in *[!0-9]*|"") prev=0 ;; esac
256: [ "$prev" -gt "$max" ] && max="$prev"
257: # The wait above can end short of CLAB_INTFS on a large lab (links attach after
258: # every container started): the NIC set still spans the expected count, and
259: # the watcher bridges the late veths.
260: case "$INTFS" in *[!0-9]*|"") INTFS=0 ;; esac
261: [ "$INTFS" -gt "$max" ] && max="$INTFS"
262: [ "$max" -gt "$prev" ] && { printf '%s\n' "$max" > "$NICS_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true; }
263: 
264: # RouterOS v7 memory ≈ 256 + 8·CPUS·(ifaces) MiB (MikroTik CHR system
265: # requirements). Scale by the HIGHEST generated NIC, not CLAB_INTFS: a sparse
266: # link on ether64 means CLAB_INTFS=1 yet 63 data NICs are created below.
267: if [ -z "${MEM:-}" ]; then
268:     MEM=$((256 + 8 * CPUS * max))
269: fi
270: 
271: bridge_eth() { # bridge_eth <i>: container ethI joins brI beside tapI (brI made once)
272:     _mtu="$(cat "$SYSNET/eth$1/mtu" 2>/dev/null || echo 1500)"
273:     if [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$1" ]; then
274:         brctl addbr "br$1"
275:         ip link set "br$1" mtu "$_mtu"
276:         ip link set "tap$1" mtu "$_mtu"
277:         # forward LLDP (01:80:c2:00:00:0e, bit 14); STP/LACP cannot cross a bridge
278:         echo 16384 > "$SYSNET/br$1/bridge/group_fwd_mask" 2>/dev/null
279:         brctl addif "br$1" "tap$1"
280:     fi
281:     brctl addif "br$1" "eth$1"
282:     ip link set "eth$1" up
283:     ip link set "br$1" up
284: }
285: # A veth that lands or returns while qemu runs (containerlab restores a link
286: # right after a restart --node, a large lab attaches late, a peer node's
287: # redeploy recreates the pair) joins its bridge as it appears, so the RouterOS
288: # interface behind tapN gets its link back without a restart here.
289: watch_links() {
290:     _warned=""
291:     while kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; do
292:         i=1
293:         while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
294:             if [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && [ ! -e "$SYSNET/br$i/brif/eth$i" ]; then
295:                 bridge_eth "$i" && log "link eth$i attached: bridged to tap$i"
296:             fi
297:             i=$((i + 1))
298:         done
299:         for d in "$SYSNET"/eth[1-9]*; do
300:             [ -e "$d" ] || continue
301:             n="${d##*/eth}"
302:             [ "$n" -gt "$max" ] || continue
303:             case " $_warned " in *" $n "*) continue ;; esac
304:             _warned="$_warned $n"
305:             log "link eth$n attached after qemu started with $max data NICs: no RouterOS interface for it until the node is restarted"
306:         done
307:         sleep 2
308:     done
309: }
310: 
311: i=1
312: while [ "$i" -le "$max" ]; do
313:     tap="tap$i"
314:     tunctl -t "$tap" >/dev/null 2>&1 || ip tuntap add dev "$tap" mode tap
315:     [ -e "$SYSNET/eth$i" ] && bridge_eth "$i"
316:     ip link set "$tap" up
317:     mac="$(printf '52:54:00:%s:%02x' "$node_id" "$((i & 255))")"
318:     NET="$NET -netdev tap,id=d$i,ifname=$tap,script=no,downscript=no -device virtio-net,netdev=d$i,mac=$mac"
319:     i=$((i + 1))
320: done
321: 
322: # shellcheck disable=SC2086
323: $QEMU $ACCEL -display none -monitor none \
324:     -m "$MEM" -smp "cpus=$CPUS" \
325:     -drive "file=$IMG,format=raw" \
326:     -serial telnet:0.0.0.0:5000,server,nowait \
327:     $NET &
328: QEMU_PID=$!
329: trap 'kill "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; wait "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; exit 0' TERM INT
330: log "qemu started (pid $QEMU_PID, mem ${MEM}M, cpus $CPUS, data nics $max)"
331: watch_links &

333: # ---- REST helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
334: json_str() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/\\/\\\\/g; s/"/\\"/g'; }
335: rest() { # rest <user:pass> <path> [json]
336:     # Basic auth in a header, never in the URL: a password containing a URI
337:     # delimiter (#, ?, /) would change where the authority ends. REST_T is the
338:     # read timeout (default 20s).
339:     _auth="Authorization: Basic $(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')"
340:     if [ $# -ge 3 ]; then
341:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "Content-Type: application/json" \
342:             --header "$_auth" --post-data "$3" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
343:     else
344:         wget -q -O- -T "${REST_T:-20}" --header "$_auth" "http://[$VM_EP]/rest/$2" 2>/dev/null
345:     fi
346: }
347: # busybox wget discards the body of an HTTP error response, and RouterOS puts
348: # its diagnosis ONLY there ({"detail":"Script Error: … (line N column M)"}; its
349: # /log stays silent). So the calls whose failure must be readable go over a raw
350: # HTTP POST through busybox nc. busybox nc exits the moment stdin hits EOF,
351: # reply or not, and RouterOS keeps the connection open despite
352: # `Connection: close`, so the request side is held open on a fifo and closed
353: # once Content-Length bytes of body have arrived.
354: resp_complete() { # resp_complete <file>: headers + Content-Length bytes of body arrived
355:     _cl="$(grep -i -m1 '^Content-Length:' "$1" 2>/dev/null | tr -dc '0-9')"
356:     [ -n "$_cl" ] || return 1
357:     grep -q -m1 '^\r*$' "$1" 2>/dev/null || return 1
358:     [ "$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$1" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" -ge "$_cl" ]
359: }
360: rest_raw() { # rest_raw <user:pass> <path> <json> <timeout-s>  -> "<status> <body>"
361:     _f="/tmp/chr-rest.$$"; rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"; mkfifo "$_f" || return 1
362:     timeout "$(( $4 + 5 ))" nc "$VM_EP" 80 <"$_f" >"$_f.out" 2>/dev/null &
363:     _pid=$!
364:     exec 7>"$_f"
365:     printf 'POST /rest/%s HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: [%s]\r\nAuthorization: Basic %s\r\nContent-Type: application/json\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\nConnection: close\r\n\r\n%s' \
366:         "$2" "$VM_LL" "$(printf '%s' "$1" | base64 | tr -d '\n')" \
367:         "$(printf '%s' "$3" | wc -c | tr -d ' ')" "$3" >&7
368:     _left=$4
369:     while kill -0 "$_pid" 2>/dev/null && ! resp_complete "$_f.out" && [ "$_left" -gt 0 ]; do
370:         sleep 1; _left=$(( _left - 1 ))
371:     done
372:     exec 7>&-
373:     wait "$_pid" 2>/dev/null
374:     _st="$(head -n1 "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r' | cut -d' ' -f2)"
375:     _body="$(sed '1,/^\r*$/d' "$_f.out" 2>/dev/null | tr -d '\r')"
376:     rm -f "$_f" "$_f.out"
377:     printf '%s %s' "${_st:-000}" "$_body"
378: }
379: # RouterOS REST returns the object/array on success and an empty body for a
380: # bare `set`: only an explicit error object is a failure here. A silently
381: # failed call is caught by the read-back checks that follow each step.
382: is_err() { case "$1" in *'"error"'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac; }
383: 
384: # ---- wait for RouterOS ----------------------------------------------------
385: waited=0
386: AUTH=""
387: # A fresh official CHR disk has ONLY the factory `admin` account (blank
388: # password): the first boot authenticates as that account whatever --username
389: # asks for, and the requested user is created below. On a restart the pair that
390: # answers is the requested user.
391: while [ -z "$AUTH" ]; do
392:     for _cred in "admin:" "admin:$PASSWORD" "$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"; do
393:         rest "$_cred" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 && { AUTH="$_cred"; break; }
394:     done
395:     [ -n "$AUTH" ] && break
396:     if ! kill -0 "$QEMU_PID" 2>/dev/null; then
397:         log "qemu exited during boot"
398:         exit 1
399:     fi
400:     sleep 2
401:     waited=$((waited + 2))
402:     if [ "$waited" -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
403:         log "RouterOS did not answer within ${BOOT_WAIT}s: leaving qemu running"
404:         wait "$QEMU_PID"
405:         exit 1
406:     fi
407: done
408: log "RouterOS answered after ${waited}s"
409: 
410: # Ready means a user can log in: RouterOS starts its SSH server well after REST
411: # answers on a slow boot (about 40 s later under TCG on arm64), so when the
412: # configuration keeps SSH enabled, its port must send the banner first.
413: # A config that disables SSH is not waited for; a banner that never comes is
414: # logged and the node is still declared ready (REST works).
415: ssh_banner() { (sleep 3) | nc "$VM_EP" 22 2>/dev/null | head -c 7; }
416: ready() {
417:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/service?name=ssh")" in
418:         *'"disabled":"false"'*)
419:             _t0=$(date +%s)
420:             until [ "$(ssh_banner)" = "SSH-2.0" ]; do
421:                 if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge "$BOOT_WAIT" ]; then
422:                     log "SSH did not answer within $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (REST works)"
423:                     break
424:                 fi
425:                 sleep 2
426:             done
427:             ;;
428:     esac
429:     touch "$READY_FILE" 2>/dev/null || true
430:     log "RouterOS ready"
431: }
432: 
433: # A failed step WITHHOLDS the ready marker (qemu keeps running, so the node can
434: # still be inspected over the serial console, port 5000 in the container).
435: bootstrap_fail() {
436:     log "credential bootstrap FAILED: $1"
437:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
438:     exit 0
439: }

441: # ---- management: ether1 addressing and its own routing table ----------------
442: # ether1 gets the container's management addresses, and their return path lives
443: # in a `mgmt` routing table selected by a rule on those source addresses: a
444: # default route the lab adds to `main` (a static 0.0.0.0/0, a PPPoE client's
445: # default route, a dual-WAN pair) would otherwise take SSH/REST replies away
446: # from the management network while the data plane works. CHR's default ether1
447: # DHCP client is disabled: the address is static. Everything is tagged
448: # clab-mgmt and re-applied on every boot from the container's CURRENT addressing
449: # (a restart can bring a new IP), while the bootstrap channel itself
450: # (link-local) never depends on it.
451: mgmt_fail() {
452:     log "management setup FAILED: $1 (redeploy the node: containerlab deploy --reconfigure)"
453:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
454:     exit 0
455: }
456: rest_has() { # rest_has <path?query>: the GET answered a non-empty JSON array
457:     case "$(rest "$AUTH" "$1")" in '['*'{'*) return 0 ;; *) return 1 ;; esac
458: }
459: rest_add() { # rest_add <what> <path> <json>: a 2xx with no error object, else mgmt_fail with the router's detail
460:     _r="$(rest_raw "$AUTH" "$2" "$3" 20)"
461:     case "$_r" in
462:         2??\ *) is_err "$_r" && mgmt_fail "$1: ${_r#* }" ;;
463:         *) mgmt_fail "$1: ${_r:-no response}" ;;
464:     esac
465: }
466: rest_count() { # rest_count <path?query>: number of objects the GET answered
467:     rest "$AUTH" "$1" | tr '{' '\n' | grep -c '"\.id"'
468: }
469: rest_clear() { # rest_clear <menu>: remove its clab-mgmt objects
470:     _ids="$(rest "$AUTH" "$1?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" | tr '{' '\n' \
471:         | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | paste -sd, -)"
472:     [ -z "$_ids" ] || rest_add "remove old $1" "$1/remove" "{\".id\":\"$_ids\"}"
473: }
474: # The tagged objects already match the container's addressing (a restart with
475: # the same IP): leave them alone, re-applying would only drop live sessions.
476: mgmt_in_place() {
477:     _want=0
478:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
479:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
480:         rest_has "routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE" || return 1
481:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_has "ip/route?routing-table=$MGMT_TABLE&dst-address=0.0.0.0/0&gateway=$G4" || return 1
482:         _want=$((_want + 1))
483:     fi
484:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
485:         rest_has "ipv6/address?interface=ether1&address=$M6&comment=$MGMT_COMMENT" || return 1
486:         _want=$((_want + 1))
487:     fi
488:     [ "$(rest_count "ip/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")$(rest_count "ipv6/address?comment=$MGMT_COMMENT")" \
489:         = "$([ -n "$M4" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)$([ -n "$M6" ] && echo 1 || echo 0)" ] || return 1
490:     rest_has "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1&ra-lifetime=none" || return 1
491:     [ "$_want" -gt 0 ]
492: }
493: mgmt_setup() {
494:     if mgmt_in_place; then
495:         log "management on ether1 unchanged: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}"
496:         return 0
497:     fi
498:     for _m in routing/rule ip/route ipv6/route ip/address ipv6/address; do rest_clear "$_m"; done
499:     rest_has "routing/table?name=$MGMT_TABLE" \
500:         || rest_add "routing table $MGMT_TABLE" routing/table/add \
501:             "{\"name\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",\"fib\":\"yes\",\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\"}"
502:     _c="\"comment\":\"$MGMT_COMMENT\""
503:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
504:         _net4="$(ipcalc -n "$M4" | sed -n 's/^NETWORK=//p')/${M4#*/}"
505:         rest_add "ether1 address $M4" ip/address/add "{\"address\":\"$M4\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",$_c}"
506:         rest_add "route $_net4 in table $MGMT_TABLE" ip/route/add \
507:             "{\"dst-address\":\"$_net4\",\"gateway\":\"ether1\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
508:         [ -z "$G4" ] || rest_add "default via $G4 in table $MGMT_TABLE" ip/route/add \
509:             "{\"dst-address\":\"0.0.0.0/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G4\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
510:         rest_add "routing rule for ${M4%/*}" routing/rule/add \
511:             "{\"src-address\":\"${M4%/*}/32\",\"action\":\"lookup-only-in-table\",\"table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
512:     fi
513:     if [ -n "$M6" ]; then
514:         rest_add "ether1 address $M6" ipv6/address/add \
515:             "{\"address\":\"$M6\",\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"advertise\":\"no\",$_c}"
516:         # RouterOS normalizes the host bits of dst-address (::3/64 -> ::/64)
517:         rest_add "IPv6 route $M6 in table $MGMT_TABLE" ipv6/route/add \
518:             "{\"dst-address\":\"$M6\",\"gateway\":\"ether1\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
519:         [ -z "$G6" ] || rest_add "IPv6 default via $G6 in table $MGMT_TABLE" ipv6/route/add \
520:             "{\"dst-address\":\"::/0\",\"gateway\":\"$G6%ether1\",\"routing-table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
521:         rest_add "routing rule for ${M6%/*}" routing/rule/add \
522:             "{\"src-address\":\"${M6%/*}/128\",\"action\":\"lookup-only-in-table\",\"table\":\"$MGMT_TABLE\",$_c}"
523:     fi
524:     _id="$(rest "$AUTH" "ip/dhcp-client?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
525:     [ -z "$_id" ] || rest_add "disable the ether1 DHCP client" ip/dhcp-client/set \
526:         "{\"numbers\":\"$_id\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}"
527:     # RouterOS's default ND entry (interface=all, ra-lifetime=30m) sends router
528:     # advertisements on ether1 too, and every host on the management network
529:     # with accept_ra would install the router as its IPv6 default route. An
530:     # ether1 entry with ra-lifetime=none keeps the RAs harmless and withdraws a
531:     # route a host already learned (a disabled entry does not override "all").
532:     # /ipv6/nd keeps no comment, so its entry is found by interface.
533:     _nd="$(rest "$AUTH" "ipv6/nd?interface=ether1" | sed -n 's/.*"\.id":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' | head -n1)"
534:     if [ -n "$_nd" ]; then
535:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/set \
536:             "{\"numbers\":\"$_nd\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\",\"disabled\":\"no\"}"
537:     else
538:         rest_add "ether1 router advertisements off" ipv6/nd/add \
539:             "{\"interface\":\"ether1\",\"ra-lifetime\":\"none\"}"
540:     fi
541:     # Prove they took (a transport flake answers an empty body, which is not
542:     # an error by the set-contract).
543:     if [ -n "$M4" ]; then
544:         rest_has "ip/address?interface=ether1&address=$M4" || mgmt_fail "$M4 not on ether1"
545:         rest_has "routing/rule?src-address=${M4%/*}/32&table=$MGMT_TABLE" \
546:             || mgmt_fail "routing rule for ${M4%/*} not applied"
547:     fi
548:     log "management on ether1: ${M4:-no IPv4}${M6:+, $M6}, return path in routing table $MGMT_TABLE"
549: }
550: # Join the management network, then have the router reach its gateway from the
551: # management address: proves the return path both ways, and the ARP/ND request
552: # refreshes the gateway's neighbor entry when the IP was used by another MAC
553: # before (a redeployed lab hands out the same addresses).
554: mgmt_attach() {
555:     [ -e "$SYSNET/$MGMT_BR/brif/eth0" ] || brctl addif "$MGMT_BR" eth0
556:     ip link set eth0 up
557:     for _pair in "$G4 ${M4%/*}" "$G6 ${M6%/*}"; do
558:         # shellcheck disable=SC2086  # split "gateway source"; an empty half skips the pair
559:         set -- $_pair
560:         [ $# -eq 2 ] || continue
561:         _t0=$(date +%s)
562:         until case "$(rest "$AUTH" ping "{\"address\":\"$1\",\"src-address\":\"$2\",\"count\":\"2\"}")" in
563:                 *'"received":"'[1-9]*) true ;; *) false ;; esac; do
564:             if [ $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 )) -ge 30 ]; then
565:                 log "gateway $1 does not answer from $2 after $(( $(date +%s) - _t0 ))s (continuing)"
566:                 break
567:             fi
568:             sleep 1
569:         done
570:     done
571: }
572: 
573: # Bootstrap + startup-config import happen ONCE per container lifetime. On a
574: # restart the CHR disk keeps its config and the marker (in the container rw
575: # layer) survives, so the bootstrap (which could wait forever if the config
576: # disabled `www` or changed the account, or reject duplicate `add` lines) is
577: # skipped. A fresh deploy recreates the container and the disk, so the marker
578: # and the config are both gone and the bootstrap runs.
579: if [ -f "$DONE_MARKER" ]; then
580:     log "already bootstrapped (restart): skipping config"
581:     mgmt_setup
582:     mgmt_attach
583:     ready
584:     wait "$QEMU_PID"
585:     exit 0
586: fi
587: 
588: # ---- credentials + identity -----------------------------------------------
589: # Every credential-establishing call is CHECKED: the ready marker never
590: # advertises credentials that do not work.
591: FACTORY="admin:"
592: rest "$FACTORY" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 || FACTORY="admin:$PASSWORD"
593: if [ "$USERNAME" = "admin" ]; then
594:     if [ -n "$PASSWORD" ]; then
595:         out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/set \
596:             "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\"}")"
597:         is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set admin password: ${out:-no response}"
598:     fi
599:     AUTH="admin:$PASSWORD"
600: else
601:     out="$(rest "$FACTORY" user/add \
602:         "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$USERNAME")\",\"password\":\"$(json_str "$PASSWORD")\",\"group\":\"full\"}")"
603:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "create user $USERNAME: ${out:-no response}"
604:     AUTH="$USERNAME:$PASSWORD"
605:     # The factory `admin` still has a BLANK password and is reachable over the
606:     # forwarded services: disable it so the node keeps no unauthenticated
607:     # full-access account.
608:     out="$(rest "$AUTH" user/set "{\"numbers\":\"admin\",\"disabled\":\"yes\"}")"
609:     is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "disable factory admin: ${out:-no response}"
610:     if rest "admin:" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1; then
611:         bootstrap_fail "factory admin still authenticates after disable"
612:     fi
613: fi
614: rest "$AUTH" system/resource >/dev/null 2>&1 \
615:     || bootstrap_fail "the requested credentials do not authenticate"
616: out="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity/set "{\"name\":\"$(json_str "$HOSTNAME_ARG")\"}")"
617: is_err "$out" && bootstrap_fail "set identity: ${out:-no response}"
618: got="$(rest "$AUTH" system/identity)"
619: case "$got" in
620:     *"\"name\":\"$HOSTNAME_ARG\""*) : ;;
621:     *) bootstrap_fail "identity not applied: ${got:-no response}" ;;
622: esac
623: 
624: mgmt_setup
625: mgmt_attach
626: 
627: # ---- startup config -------------------------------------------------------
628: if [ -s "$STARTUP_CFG" ]; then
629:     bridge_ll
630:     # one-shot HTTP server on the bridge's link-local address; the router
631:     # fetches from it through ether1 (fetch takes a zoned link-local address
632:     # only as `address=`, not inside a URL)
633:     {
634:         printf 'HTTP/1.0 200 OK\r\nContent-Type: text/plain\r\nContent-Length: %s\r\n\r\n' \
635:             "$(wc -c < "$STARTUP_CFG")"
636:         cat "$STARTUP_CFG"
637:     } | timeout 90 nc -l -s "$LL%$MGMT_BR" -p "$FETCH_PORT" >/dev/null 2>&1 &
638:     sleep 1
639:     fetch="$(rest "$AUTH" tool/fetch \
640:         "{\"address\":\"$LL%ether1\",\"port\":\"$FETCH_PORT\",\"src-path\":\"/config.auto.rsc\",\"mode\":\"http\",\"dst-path\":\"config.auto.rsc\"}")"
641:     case "$fetch" in
642:         *'"status":"finished"'*)
643:             # /import answers only when it finishes: a large config gets
644:             # CHR_BOOT_WAIT seconds.
645:             result="$(rest_raw "$AUTH" import '{"file-name":"config.auto.rsc"}' "$BOOT_WAIT")"
646:             case "$result" in
647:                 *'"ret":"true"'*)
648:                     log "startup config imported"
649:                     ;;
650:                 *)
651:                     # RouterOS imports line by line and stops at the first
652:                     # error: the lines before it ARE applied.
653:                     detail="$(printf '%s' "$result" | sed -n 's/.*"detail":"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p')"
654:                     log "startup config import FAILED: ${detail:-${result:-no response}}; lines before the failing one were applied, the rest were not"
655:                     wait "$QEMU_PID"
656:                     exit 0
657:                     ;;
658:             esac
659:             ;;
660:         *)
661:             log "startup config import FAILED: fetch did not finish: ${fetch:-no response}"
662:             wait "$QEMU_PID"
663:             exit 0
664:             ;;
665:     esac
666: fi
667: 
668: touch "$DONE_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true
669: ready
670: wait "$QEMU_PID"

(End of file - total 670 lines)
